chats.answer:
For Time Machine backups from 2–3 Macs, I'd prioritize reliability, macOS compatibility, quiet operation, and easy recovery over raw NAS performance.

My top recommendation is Synology, particularly its Plus-series 2-bay NAS models. Synology's software makes it relatively easy to create separate Time Machine backup destinations for multiple Macs, set storage quotas, and monitor drive health.

I'd use two NAS-rated hard drives in a RAID 1 mirror, connect the NAS to your router or Ethernet switch, and let each Mac back up over Wi-Fi or Ethernet.

One important distinction: RAID 1 protects against a single drive failure, but it doesn't replace having another backup of your most important files.

My top 3 picks

1. Synology DiskStation DS225+ 2-Bay NAS Enclosure

Best overall
$364.99

Intel processor, 2GB RAM, 2.5GbE Ethernet. Great if you want Time Machine plus future file or photo storage.

Diskless · B&H Photo

2. Synology DiskStation DS223 2-Bay NAS Enclosure

Best value for Time Machine
$304.99

2GB RAM, 1GbE Ethernet. Plenty for automated backups from a couple of Macs. This is probably all you actually need.

Diskless · B&H Photo

3. Synology DiskStation DS223j 2-Bay (Diskless)

Budget choice

1GB RAM, 1GbE Ethernet. Good for dedicated Time Machine use, though with less headroom for additional applications.

Diskless · Adorama

Synology documents Time Machine support over SMB, and Apple recommends SMB rather than the older AFP protocol.

For backup-only use, NAS-rated CMR hard drives are a sensible choice. SSDs generally aren't worth the extra cost.

What I'd buy

Synology DS223 with 2 × 8TB NAS hard drives if the NAS is exclusively for Time Machine. The DS225+ is worth the extra money if you want faster networking or anticipate other uses.

Configure a separate SMB Time Machine destination and quota for each Mac, enable Time Machine encryption on the Macs, and periodically test restoring a file.

One question that would help narrow this down: How much storage do your Macs have in total? For example, two 1TB MacBooks, or a 2TB Mac Studio plus a 512GB MacBook. That will determine whether 4TB, 6TB, or 8TB drives make the most sense.
